scope: Palette-only refinement on fixed cleaned labels, exact RGB lookup reuse, 256-label fix, honest opaque-counter diagnostics; no new satin or background segmentation claims.

protocol.public_suite: uv run python scripts/benchmark_interpretation.py --suite public --machine --check --baseline-ref main --previous-ref 4f4d6fb --output output/benchmark-quality
protocol.performance: Same script/corpus with --mode performance --warmups 1 --repeats 3 --machine --check, sequential main -> previous -> candidate; isolated fresh worker per input/reference; one warm-up plus three timed generate() calls.
protocol.timing_scope: Full library generate including exports; imports, hashes, SVG oracle rendering and PES/DST readbacks outside timing. No project tests/builds/other generations during the measurement protocol; idle API/Next and static completed preview remained open. Host is shared.
protocol.fidelity_scope: Synthetic source oracles before encoding/background, source-coordinate mapping with pixel centres, no bbox fitting. Private inputs have no invented semantic oracle. ΔE76 colour tolerance 14.
protocol.thread_model_distinction: Machine source oracle draws nominal 0.4 mm top-thread lines with source-grid boundary tolerance. Engine structural/literal coverage statistics retain their own 0.3 mm thread model and 0.25 mm structural tolerance; these metrics are different and neither is physical sewout.
protocol.gating: --check rejects unexpected outcomes, trace boundary failures, nondeterminism and failed machine safety checks. Fidelity scores remain descriptive, including known failures.
protocol.memory_scope: ru_maxrss is whole worker including imports/native allocations/warm-up, not only the timed function. Helper tracemalloc allocation measurement is separate.
protocol.private_inputs: Local user artwork not published. Source hashes and physical parameters are recorded; repeat requires those exact inputs.
protocol.limits: Procedural and logo corpus, no broad real-photo corpus and no physical PP1 sewout. Three timings/p95 and fixed phase order on a shared Mac do not establish causal speedup or a performance SLA.
